<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XIX.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|193}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=19|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel in the Dedication of a Church, & Anniversary thereof.}}entring in, he vvalked through Iericho. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=2}}† And behold a man named Zachaeus: and this vvas a Prince of the Publicans, and he riche. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=3}}† And he sought to see {{sc|Iesvs}} vvhat he vvas, and he could not for the multitude, because he vvas litle of stature. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=4}}† And running before, he {{sup|‖}} vvent vp into a sycomore tree that he might see him: because he vvas to passe by it. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=5}}† And vvhen he vvas come to the place, {{sc|Iesvs}} looking vp, savv him, and said to him, Zachaeus, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Zachæus.}}∷ come dovvne in hast: because this day I must abide in thy house. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=6}}† And he in hast came dovvne, and receiued him reioycing. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=7}}† And vvhen al savv it, they murmured, saying that he turned in, to a man that vvas a sinner. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=8}}† But Zachaeus standing, said to our Lord, Behold the halfe of my goods, Lord, I giue to the poore: and if I haue defrauded any man of any thing, {{sup|‖}} I restore fourefold. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=9}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, That this day saluation is made to this house: because that he also is the sonne of Abraham. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=10}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 18, 12.''}}* For the Sonne of man is come to seeke and to saue that vvhich vvas lost.⊣

{{verse|chapter=19|verse=11}}† They hearing these things, he added and spake a parable, for that he was nigh to Hierusalem, and because they thought that forthvvith the kingdom of God should be manifested. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=12}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 25, 14.''}}* He said therfore, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel for S. Lewis the King of France, August 25. And for some other Confessors not Bishops.}}A certaine noble man vvent into a farre countrie to take to him self a kingdom, and to returne. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=13}}† And calling his ten seruants, he gaue them ten poundes, and said to them, Occupie til I come. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=14}}† And his citizens hated him: and they sent a legacie after him, saying, VVe vvil not haue this man reigne ouer vs. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=15}}† And it came to passe after he returned, hauing receiued his kingdom: and he commaunded his seruants to be called, to vvhom he gaue the money: that he might knovv how much euery man had gained by occupying. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=16}}† And the first came, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gotten ten poundes. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=17}}† And he said to him, VVel fare thee good seruant, because thou hast been faithful in a litle, thou shalt haue povver ouer {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Marke here against the aduersaries, that the rewards of these two good seruants be diuers & vnaequal, according to the diuersitie or inequality of their gaines, that is, their merites. and yet one receiueth the peny ''(Mt. 20, 9''.) as wel as the other, that is, heauen or life euerlasting.}}∷ ten cities. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=18}}† And the second came, saying, Lord, thy pound hath made fiue poundes. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=19}}† And he said to him, And be thou ouer fiue cities. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=20}}† And an other came, saying, Lord, loe here thy pound, vvhich I haue had laid vp in a napkin. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=21}}† for I feared thee, because thou art an austêre man: thou takest vp that thou didst not set dovvne, and thou reapest<noinclude>{{rh||Bb|that}}</noinclude>
